dedupe_keys.name: targeted cooling of new york city cycling networks in the june 2024 heatwave

description: This study quantifies how hot cyclists get in New York City and where cooling would help most. Agustin Cabrera, David Ziegler and Markus Schläpfer coupled a high-resolution urban microclimate chain (the WRF model with the BEP urban scheme, downscaled with SOLWEIG for mean radiant temperature) with 4.76 million Citi Bike trips during the June 2024 heatwave, routed on the street network. They found that a small fraction of streets concentrates most rider heat exposure; targeted tree planting on 1.5 percent of the network reduced heat-exposed kilometres ridden by 19 percent, equal to about 4 degrees C less thermal stress, mostly at midday, while random planting across the city gave diffuse and costly cooling. Daytime heat stress was higher in lower-income neighbourhoods. Coverage: New York City, one heatwave in June 2024. Access: arXiv preprint from December 2025 with data and code on Zenodo. Licence and cost: the paper is CC BY 4.0 and free. Caveats: a preprint not yet peer reviewed; trip routes are inferred from start and end stations; the tree scenario is modelled, not built; and only docked Citi Bike trips are covered. It is useful for climate adaptation and heat exposure planning of cycling networks. It used the Citi Bike system data and SOLWEIG, part of the UMEP platform, both catalogued here.
